candidate.text: # Measurement check

An offline Python utility for reviewing the supplied mass-comparison records and optical reference controls. It recalculates the limits from the input records and settings; it does not contain a table of expected exceptions.
## Run
Install the packages in `requirements.txt` in the Python environment. No network connection is used by the utility itself.

```sh
python /workspace/output/measurement-check/measurement_check.py --mass /workspace/input/instrument-history/mass-checks.csv --optical /workspace/input/instrument-history/optical-checks.csv --config /workspace/input/instrument-history/control-settings.json --output /workspace/output/
```

All four paths are explicit. Quote paths containing spaces. Input row and column order do not affect the result; Record IDs identify measurements. The output directory is created if necessary. A successful run writes `review-results.json` and `exceptions.csv`, replacing files with those names in the selected output directory, and prints the summary. An input error returns a nonzero exit code with a message on stderr. Run each review into a fresh directory to keep earlier results separate.

The published `measurement-interface.json` describes the CSV columns, result fields and status codes. CSV input is UTF-8, with or without a BOM. Each mass input describes a single balance, check-standard and design combination; mixed or blank system identifiers are rejected. The utility rejects duplicate or missing Record IDs, nonfinite measurements, negative residual SD, incomplete daily reference groups, invalid control parameters and an unsupported family method.
## Calculation basis

The baseline is defined by decimal year strictly below the configured cutoff. Monitoring records are excluded from that baseline; repeated decimal years remain separate runs. The sample SD uses n−1. Residual variances are pooled with their degrees of freedom before taking the square root. The upper precision limit uses the upper-tail F probability, with single-run degrees in the numerator and actual baseline degrees in the denominator. A baseline exception is retained and marked for investigation rather than silently removed.

For the optical system, the forward relation is Y=a+bX. Corrected width is `(Y-a)/b`; control error is corrected width minus reference width. The simultaneous two-sided t probability is derived from the configured Sidak family significance and group size. Residual SD is converted to the width scale using the absolute slope. Equality to either control limit is within limits. If any reference fails, the daily result requires repeat measurement of the linked workload; the tool does not turn reference-control counts into customer-work counts.

`exceptions.csv` contains one row per failing metric. A mass run failing two metrics would appear twice there but once in the summary exception count. The one-sided residual-SD check has a blank lower limit. `review-results.json` includes every received record, each observed optical day, the reconstructed baseline and the monitoring trend, so passing records remain inspectable.
## Reading the supplied records

The received mass series gives 99 baseline records and 118 monitoring records, with 297 baseline residual degrees. The legacy 117/351 entry is retained for reconciliation; the discrepancy does not establish that 18 records were lost. M047 is a historical baseline precision exception. Monitoring runs M129, M154, M179 and M207 require repeat-work review. Optical controls L010-L012 fail on day 4, so the corresponding daily result identifies that linked-work scope.

The monitoring mean lies above the baseline mean, and 97 of 118 monitoring values exceed the baseline mean. This supports review of process change even though most individual checks are within limits. It does not identify a particular failed component or justify rejecting every measurement.
## Applicability

Retaining M047 follows the fixed historical reconstruction rule; it does not certify a stable baseline for future work. Before operational reuse, reconcile that run and the legacy population, assess process stability, and obtain technical approval for the reference limits. The variance and t-based procedures also rely on suitable measurement-distribution and independence assumptions; calculating a limit does not validate those assumptions.

The optical checks exercise the supplied linear calibration at 0.76, 3.29 and 8.89 µm. They do not establish validity outside that checked range or supply missing product tolerances. The configured family significance applies to the reference group within a checking period, not to every result across the entire archive.
## Evidence limits

No complete client-work register, product tolerances, uncertainty-based acceptance data, repair history or completed remeasurement evidence accompanies these files. `affected_customer_work_count` is therefore null, `product_conformity` remains `not_determined`, and completed remeasurement is not confirmed. A later passing control does not establish that earlier work was repaired or repeated.

For retrospective use, retrieve the affected runs' work orders and result-use links, the full day-4 workload register, and any subsequent repeat and authorization records. A known linked item does not prove complete coverage of the affected group. Baseline reconciliation and M047's historical action need their own supporting records. Closure requires valid repeat results and technical authorization; this utility provides statistical checks and evidence pointers, not product release approval.

source_materials.text: Mass comparison and optical linewidth control
Mass system: Balance 12; check standard 41; calibration design 41.
Record set: 217 mass-comparison records and 18 optical reference controls. The two systems are independent.

The instrument-history folder contains mass-checks.csv, optical-checks.csv and control-settings.json. The mass records retain the original decimal-year precision; different Record IDs at the same decimal year represent separate runs. Optical day numbers identify a separate control series and have no established calendar relationship to the mass records. The file interface for the utility is defined in measurement-interface.json.

Use all received records strictly before the configured cutoff year as the fixed baseline, and later records as the monitoring series. Historical baseline exceptions remain in this calculation and are investigated separately. The legacy summary lists 117 baseline records and 351 residual degrees of freedom; its corresponding record population has not been reconciled.

The signed check-value limits are the baseline mean plus or minus the configured multiple of the sample standard deviation. Pool residual variances using their degrees of freedom, then take the square root. The precision upper limit uses the configured upper-tail F significance, with single-run degrees in the numerator and reconstructed baseline degrees in the denominator. Equality with a limit is within limits.

The initial calibration relates response Y to width X by Y=a+bX. Convert the response to the width scale; report control error as corrected width minus reference width. The original fit used 40 measurements on 10 references; those individual fit measurements are not included in the transfer.

Each day is qualified by the configured reference group using a Sidak simultaneous two-sided t limit. Use the configured familywise significance and fit degrees of freedom. The absolute limit equals residual SD divided by absolute slope, multiplied by the critical value. Any failing reference control requires remeasurement of the workload linked to that control day.

Client work orders, product specifications, uncertainty evaluations, repair history and completed remeasurements must be retrieved separately. Single-record checks do not establish long-term process stability or product acceptance. The affected customer-work count remains unknown without complete workload links; later passing controls alone do not prove correction of earlier work.

---
name: bound-retrospective-impact
description: Turn detected process or quality failures into evidence-bounded historical impact and follow-up decisions when workload links are incomplete.
---

Build a chain from observed failure to applicable decision scope to identifiable affected records. Keep confirmed affected items, items requiring investigation and absent evidence distinct. Read [scope and closure](references/scope-and-closure.md) before extending a run-level finding to a day, shipment, product or client.

Use [propagate_groups.py](scripts/propagate_groups.py) only when the supplied procedure authorizes a group-level consequence and a real linking key is present. The helper returns known record IDs and unresolved groups; it never manufactures missing workload items.

Test both overreach and omission: a failed control may implicate known associated work, but incomplete links do not justify either declaring everything safe or inventing a precise affected quantity. Recommendations may differ while preserving the same evidence boundaries and closure conditions.

Completeness is separate evidence: a single valid link proves that item is associated, not that every associated item is listed. Supply `documented_complete_groups` only for groups whose full workload coverage is explicitly established by an authoritative register or closure evidence. Omitted coverage leaves the group unresolved even when known items exist; an invalid item in a declared complete group also leaves it unresolved. The helper cannot verify the truth of the completeness declaration.

# Scope and closure

For each adopted claim record: system, measurement period, failure criterion, supplied linking evidence, affected record set and confidence. A timestamp alone is not necessarily a unique event key. Distinguish control artifacts from customer workload and process qualification from product specifications.

Use three outcomes when evidence warrants them: a confirmed action, a conditional action awaiting a named record, or no supported extension beyond the observed check. A missing history is not a zero count. Differences between two reported populations may reflect scope or a missing attachment; they do not identify missing individual records.

An actionable follow-up names who should retrieve which evidence and what closes the issue. Examples include approved repeat results, an authoritative work-order association or a formally authorized change to the process baseline. Later passing checks do not by themselves close earlier failures. Do not attribute cause from a pattern alone.

Keep an audit distinction between retaining a recorded pointwise pass and approving the entire process for a new use. Reports should make that distinction understandable without requiring the reader to know statistical terminology.

Completeness is separate evidence: a single valid link proves that item is associated, not that every associated item is listed. Supply `documented_complete_groups` only for groups whose full workload coverage is explicitly established by an authoritative register or closure evidence. Omitted coverage leaves the group unresolved even when known items exist; an invalid item in a declared complete group also leaves it unresolved. The helper cannot verify the truth of the completeness declaration.

name: review-measurement-control
description: Reconstruct measurement-control baselines and evaluate instrument checks with the correct scale, degrees of freedom and grouped decision rule.
---

Separate measurement records from the approved control rule before calculating limits. Identify the reference regime, instrument, unit, baseline membership and independent record key. A printed sample count is a claim to reconcile, not a substitute for reconstructing the baseline.

Read [baseline discipline](references/baselines.md) when old summary cards conflict with raw records or later observations are available. Read [scale and grouped checks](references/scale-and-groups.md) when instruments use fitted correction curves or several reference points jointly qualify a run.

Use [control_limits.py](scripts/control_limits.py) for transparent pooled-repeatability and simultaneous-control calculations. Pass all parameters explicitly. The helper does not choose a baseline, validate an instrument, or authorize removal of records.

For a reusable command-line tool, read [rerunnable checks](references/rerunnable-checks.md). Validate method selectors and incomplete groups, then challenge the tool with both representation changes and changed measurements.

Verify signed intermediate values as well as final flags. An absolute-value decision can conceal a reversed correction sign. Report pointwise failures, process-pattern evidence and missing workload links separately. Do not infer product acceptance from process control alone.

# Baseline discipline

Freeze a baseline by the approved membership rule before examining monitoring outcomes. Use an explicit record identifier: repeated timestamps can represent distinct runs. Reconcile observed membership with legacy counts and degrees of freedom. An unexplained count difference is not proof that specific records were lost.

Pool residual variances using their degrees of freedom, then take the square root. Averaging standard deviations is different. The denominator degrees of freedom comes from the actual accepted baseline, not an unrelated summary card. A variance-control limit is generally one-sided; a signed bias limit can be two-sided.

Do not silently include monitoring data or discard baseline outliers to make a chart pass. If the baseline itself has questionable records, retain the prescribed calculation, identify the concern and distinguish a formally approved replacement baseline from an exploratory sensitivity check.

Useful checks: reorder source rows; retain different records with the same timestamp; recompute on changed values; test unequal residual degrees of freedom; compare fixed-baseline and all-data limits. Label derived probes as probes, not original-data failures.

# Rerunnable measurement checks

A reusable tool must read the current records and settings rather than replay a previously verified answer. Separate parsing, parameter validation, calculations and serialization so each stage can be challenged independently.

Treat a configured method name as an executable contract. Reject unsupported selectors explicitly; silently falling back to the only implemented method can return convincing numbers under an incorrect declared procedure. Validate domain constraints and group completeness before writing success artifacts.

Use metamorphic checks to test dependence on the evidence: reorder rows and columns, rename record IDs, move files to paths containing spaces, change a baseline observation, introduce a new monitoring exception and alter a calibration coefficient. Invariance under representation changes and appropriate changes under substantive inputs are different obligations. Reconstruct the expected results independently for changed inputs.

Keep record-level failures, failing metrics and affected groups separate. One record may fail two metrics; several failed references may identify one affected period. Unknown downstream workload stays unknown until complete linkage evidence is supplied. Direct CLI tests are implementation validation, not evidence of model improvement.

Probe small, valid tail probabilities. Forming `1-alpha` or subtracting two nearly equal probabilities can round a finite tail to zero before quantile inversion. Use stable complement/inverse-survival formulations and `log1p`/`expm1` for grouped probabilities. Cross-check with a different numerical route, such as solving the log-survival equation; merely calling a similarly implemented inverse in a second script may repeat the same defect.

Before pooling records, validate the identity of the measured system, reference standard and method/design. Either calculate independently for each supported group or explicitly reject mixed groups; a shared unit does not make distinct instruments one process.

# Scale and grouped checks

Write the forward calibration equation and units before inverting it. For response y = a + b x, infer x from (y-a)/b. Name the sign convention of the reported discrepancy; a correction and an error can have opposite signs. Convert the residual uncertainty to the same scale as the discrepancy before applying a threshold.

A procedure may control a group of reference points rather than independent pointwise decisions. Derive the critical probability from the declared family error rule; do not replace it with a familiar single-point interval. Keep full precision until the final comparison and state whether equality is accepted.

A failing reference point can invalidate an entire run or period only when the procedure establishes that scope. Passing checks later do not establish that earlier workload items were repeated or repaired. A descriptive shift in many individually passing values warrants process review, without proving a particular physical failure mode.

scope: Content-only review of README, supplied-run JSON and exceptions. Complete source CSV rows are included. Independent execution verifies all records and altered-input cases. JSON excerpts include summaries, limits, daily scope, trends and failures; infer no unshown candidate values.
